facts.raw_span: 3-year history of a complex progressive disorder
Emotional lability
Cognitive decline
Generalized ataxia
Autonomic dysfunction
Patient denied paresthesias, dysesthesias, or loss of sensation
Abnormal cardiac parasympathetic function (without orthostatic hypotension)
Patchy decrease in sweat output on quantitative sudomotor axon reflex test
Markedly abnormal thermoregulatory sweat test with near complete global anhidrosis
α-galactosidase activity: 0.056 U/L (normal range: 0.074-0.457 U/L)
Elevated protein levels (95 mg/dL) in cerebrospinal fluid analysis
Bilateral hyperintensity in the pulvinar region of thalami and global diffuse brain volume loss on MRI Brain

concepts.why: The patient's low alpha-galactosidase activity, abnormal thermoregulatory sweat test, and bilateral hyperintensity in the pulvinar region of thalami are consistent with Fabry disease.
The patient's generalized ataxia, autonomic dysfunction, and abnormal cardiac parasympathetic function are consistent with multiple system atrophy.
The patient's cognitive decline, emotional lability, and bilateral hyperintensity in the pulvinar region of thalami are consistent with frontotemporal dementia.
The patient's autonomic dysfunction, abnormal cardiac parasympathetic function, and patchy decrease in sweat output are consistent with autonomic failure.
The patient's generalized ataxia and bilateral hyperintensity in the pulvinar region of thalami are consistent with cerebellar ataxia.
The patient's cognitive decline, emotional lability, and bilateral hyperintensity in the pulvinar region of thalami are consistent with Lewy body dementia.
The patient's generalized ataxia, autonomic dysfunction, and bilateral hyperintensity in the pulvinar region of thalami are consistent with mitochondrial neurogastrointestinal encephalomyopathy.
The patient's cognitive decline, emotional lability, and bilateral hyperintensity in the pulvinar region of thalami are consistent with toxic encephalopathy.
